details.description: Tev1-4B-experimental is Together AI's experimental decision-classifier model, a supervised fine-tune of Alibaba's Qwen3.5-4B built to select exactly one option from a structured state, question, and list of 2 to 24 labeled choices, returning only that option's letter. Together's Hugging Face model card describes it as a 'Jev-inspired experiment' that keeps Qwen's standard next-token language-model head rather than a separate non-autoregressive runtime, and recommends a fixed system prompt with temperature 0 and an 8-token output cap for its intended use. On Together's own development evaluation the model chose the correct option in 880 of 1,000 cases (88.0%) on its main decision set and 300 of 300 (100%) on a synthetic policy-transfer set, though Together's card states these are development results, not an independent benchmark, and that no untuned-Qwen baseline exists yet for comparison.
advantages: On Together AI's own development evaluation, the model selected the correct option in 880 of 1,000 cases (88.0%) on the main decision set, per Together's Hugging Face model card.

On the same development evaluation, the model matched 300 of 300 (100%) cases on a synthetic policy-transfer set and produced a valid single-letter output in all 1,300 evaluation calls with zero HTTP errors, per Together's model card.

Built specifically for structured decision and classification tasks (choosing one labeled option from 2-24 choices) rather than general chat, with a documented recommended prompt template and request parameters, per Together's model card.
Retains Qwen's standard next-token language-model head, so it can be served with the same inference stacks (Transformers, vLLM, SGLang) as its Qwen3.5-4B base, per Together's model card.
disadvantages: Together's own model card states its 88.0%/100% figures come from a development-stage evaluation, not an independent benchmark, and that no untuned-Qwen baseline yet exists for comparison.
Together's model card states generic chat is not the intended interface and may produce prose.
Together's model card states the model can be wrong and should not be used as the sole authority for high-impact decisions.
Together's model card states prompt injection, multilingual behavior, calibration, and broad out-of-distribution robustness have not been comprehensively evaluated.
Labeled 'experimental' by Together AI; its model card also states the release license for these fine-tuned weights is still being finalized.
use_cases: Structured decision and classification tasks where the input is a state, a question, and a small set of labeled options, and the output is a single option letter, per Together's model card.
Policy or rule-based decision automation, based on the model's 100% match rate on Together's synthetic policy-transfer evaluation set, per Together's model card.
Low-latency single-token classification calls, given the recommended 8-token output cap and temperature-0 (deterministic) sampling, per Together's model card.

sources.title: How to train your own Jev - Together AI

notes: Left 'evaluations' empty: the only quantitative results the maker publishes (880/1,000 and 300/300 on Together's own development sets) are explicitly labeled by Together's model card as 'development results, not an independent benchmark' with 'no untuned-Qwen baseline yet,' so they are reported as advantages with that caveat rather than as leaderboard-style accuracy entries. The model card tags this model 'image-text-to-text' and its base (Qwen3.5-4B) appears to be multimodal, and the card lists 'Model size: 5B params' despite the '4B' name, but the catalog's modality for this URI is text_input/text_output only; kept the catalog's modality as authoritative and did not describe image input. Catalog's max_input_tokens (32,768) is not contradicted by any figure on the model card, which does not state a context length.
